subject.title: [Feature]: openclaw notify — admin-scoped push to connected UI sessions

question: Should OpenClaw add a core `openclaw notify` admin broadcast surface now, fold it into the broader WebUI notification architecture, or leave shell-originated alerts to plugin/external delivery paths?
rationale: The requested behavior is absent, but adding it defines a new shell-facing admin capability that affects Gateway authorization, visible UI interruption policy, and notification UX.

options.title: Design Core Notify Contract
options.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical CLI/Gateway/Control UI feature and require an explicit admin event/RPC contract before implementation.

options.title: Fold Into WebUI Notifications
options.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/20237 own the broader UI architecture and supersede this issue only after it explicitly covers shell/admin broadcast.

options.title: Prefer Plugin Or External Delivery
options.body: Reject a core command and document the supported plugin, channel, or Web Push workaround if maintainers decide shell-originated alerts should not directly interrupt Control UI sessions.

recommendation.title: Design Core Notify Contract
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical CLI/Gateway/Control UI feature and require an explicit admin event/RPC contract before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter is the best available routing owner from current-main history across the CLI, Gateway broadcast, Web Push, and Control UI surfaces involved in the decision.
